description:
We are a team based in Antofagasta, Chile, passionate about technology, innovation, science, and solving real-world challenges.

We are looking for motivated, curious, and collaborative individuals with an interest in areas such as programming, artificial intelligence, data analysis, engineering, and scientific research.

Let's combine our ideas, build something meaningful, and represent Antofagasta in this global challenge! 🚀
summary: The app was designed to help farmers make decisions based on environmental and soil data. The app’s various sections allow users to view conditions in a specific area. Based on this information, users can determine whether the current crop is suitable for the prevailing conditions (such as rainfall, heat, etc.). The app also allows you to compare crop rotations, meaning you can see which crop is best to plant after the current one. There is also a section that uses available data to predict which crops will perform best over time based on your desired strategy (productivity, balance, or resilience).
details:
This project aims to facilitate decision-making for farmers when they want to rotate their crops; the idea is to help them decide which crop to grow in the next season. The purpose of this is to help maintain soil health and conserve water and financial resources. Python, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript were used, along with various Python libraries such as Pandas, NumPy, and SciPy, as well as other technologies like Flask and Leaflet for map visualization, among others.

The benefits of crop rotation based on local climate and soil data are that it allows farmers to choose their next crop while considering how much water it will consume, how it will affect soil health, and other factors—such as how resilient the crops will be to future conditions based on historical records.

The project’s creativity stems from incorporating a variety of tools, such as optimization models, statistical methods, and real historical data from a U.S. county. All of this was integrated into a single app, resulting in a functional prototype.
